intro: The excavators broke the seal on a tomb that appears on no dynasty list. Every chamber is empty except for a single inscription, carved in a script that is not quite hieroglyphic, and in each recess beside it a small clay token rests on a stone ledge, its face stamped with a single sign. One of the diggers, who keeps the season's accounts, has begun copying the signs into a ledger, and the ink is still damp where she notes that every token bears two marks: the mark of its chamber, and a second mark that grows larger as she moves deeper into the rock.
echo: A single needle of granite; London, Paris and New York each carried one home.

puzzles.title: False Door
puzzles.flavor: Stopped hands, raised arms. It was written down last letter first.

partials.0b653e36ae9c795b4eff34beae6bd20cb9ee18f9: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: Imagine each of these as a person holding two flags out at arm's length. Sailors had an alphabet for that. And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.
Flag semaphore: the two hands are the two arms, and each pair of angles is a letter. Then one more layer: Read what you get backwards.

puzzles.title: Field Of Reeds
puzzles.flavor: Thumbs, patience, and no predictive text.
hints: Two frequencies at once is the sound of a phone key being pressed. What letters did those keys carry?
Old phone keypads: find each key, then press it the number of times shown to move along its letters.

puzzles.title: Weighing Of The Heart
puzzles.flavor: Each column remembers what it held, but not in what order.
hints: Black squares are spaces. Which two- and three-letter words fit, using only the letters each column allows?
Each column's letters drop into that column of the grid; cross them off as you place them. The sentence tells you what to submit.

puzzles.title: The Rosetta Problem
puzzles.flavor: Pairs of numbers pencilled in the margin. Start from the end; that's where it started.

blocks.text: The excavators broke the seal on a tomb that appears on no dynasty list. Every chamber is empty except for a single inscription, carved in a script that is not quite hieroglyphic.

partials.f828151241e1484917a37c445032a6b0ee2e69b6: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: The first number in each pair never goes past the number of words on the page. What does the second count? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.
The first number finds a word on the page; the second finds a letter in it. Then one more layer: Read what you get backwards.

puzzles.title: Hall Of Records
puzzles.flavor: It never travels in a straight line, and neither does the truth.

blocks.text: The knight sets out from a7: Nb5 Nc7 Ne8 Nf6 Nh5 Ng7 Ne6 Nc5 Nd3.

hints: Those are chess moves. Which squares does the piece land on, and what's written there?
Start on the given square, play each move, and read the letter on every square it lands on.

puzzles.title: Canopic Jars
puzzles.flavor: Up and down, up and down, and not a single space left.

blocks.text: WDYAW TWEDP NVIYO NOELO EOMYO WIEON HWRTM LADOE UELOT TEETN LNUNR DTOEE MQTNH XE

hints: All the right letters are here, just out of order. Could they have been written along a path that goes up and down?
Rail fence: written in a zigzag over a few rows, then copied out row by row. Try two to five rows.

meta.title: Meta: Valley Of The Kings
hints: Every entry has two numbers. What in this round is numbered, and what could the second number count?
The first number picks a puzzle; the second picks a letter inside its answer.
